jobs.description:

With built-in governance, auditability, and human oversight, Camunda gives enterprises the control they need to move AI from pilots to production — safely and at scale. Trusted by over 700 organizations worldwide, including 9 of top 10 US banks, Camunda helps enterprises boost operational efficiency, accelerate time-to-value, and deliver better customer experiences.

Fully remote and global, we are in the middle of something bigger: transforming into an AI-first organisation, built on our own platform. We use Agentic AI to automate, orchestrate intelligent processes, and elevate human contribution across every team.

Named GP Bullhound’s Top 100 Next Unicorn list, 2025 Great Place to Work certified. Visionary in 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. ranked 3rd in Flexa's 2026 Most Flexible Companies, We’re growing fast and looking for top talent to join our team. If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading.

About the role:

We're looking for a Senior Site Reliability Engineer who's passionate about building reliable, scalable infrastructure that helps developers ship better software faster. You'll design and maintain our Kubernetes-based multi-cloud platform, improve our monitoring and observability tools, and collaborate with product and engineering teams to solve real problems in real time. This is a role where you'll own the systems that power Camunda, drive automation that raises the bar for everyone, and mentor others who want to do the same. If you thrive on building things that work well and don't break when they shouldn't, we'd love to talk.

What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Design and maintain our infrastructure – You'll evolve our Kubernetes-based, multi-cloud platform architecture, ensuring it's available, scalable, and fault-tolerant. You'll establish configuration best practices and network services that our teams rely on.

  • Build observability that matters – Implement and improve monitoring and alerting tools that give both SREs and developers real visibility into system health and performance. Make it easy for teams to understand what's happening across our stack.

  • Own your systems end-to-end – You'll adopt a "you build it, you run it" mentality, which means participating in on-call rotations and being the go-to person when things need quick fixes. You'll create runbooks and automation that turn complex problems into manageable processes.

  • Ship features and improvements with product teams – Work cross-functionally with product engineering, product management, and support to define and deliver features that move the needle. Bring your expertise to the table early and often.

  • Push automation to the next level – Identify repetitive work and automate it away. Share what you learn with your teammates so everyone gets better at their craft. We measure progress by the quality of our systems, not hours worked.

  • Be the expert others learn from – Help less experienced engineers tackle complex infrastructure challenges. Break down technical problems into clear steps and support others in growing their skills. 

What You Bring:

Must Haves:

  • Deep hands-on experience with Kubernetes – You've built, deployed, and maintained Kubernetes clusters in production environments. You understand how to manage workloads, networking, and storage at scale.

  • Infrastructure as code expertise – You're fluent in tools like Terraform (or similar IaC tools) and know how to version, test, and safely deploy infrastructure changes.

  • Demonstrated experience in monitoring and observability – You've worked with tools like Prometheus, Grafana, or similar platforms to instrument systems and alert on what matters.

  • Strong 3rd-level support and incident response skills – You've responded to production incidents, diagnosed complex issues, and communicated clearly with stakeholders under pressure. You understand root cause analysis and how to prevent issues from happening again.

  • A passion for automation and raising the quality bar – You see manual work as a problem to be solved. You care deeply about building systems that are reliable, maintainable, and easy to understand.

  • Responsible use of AI tools – You leverage AI for research, code review, documentation, test generation, and automation to improve your effectiveness. You know how to validate AI outputs against requirements, never share confidential or personal data with AI systems without authorization, and always retain human accountability for decisions and deliverables.

 Nice-to-haves:

  • Experience with major cloud providers – You've worked with AWS (EKS), Google Cloud Platform (GKE), or similar managed Kubernetes services.

  • ArgoCD or GitOps workflows – You've used declarative, Git-driven infrastructure management to keep systems in sync.

  • Proficiency in Python, Go, or similar languages – You write scripts and automation tools that solve real problems.

  • Experience with SLOs and alerting frameworks – You've helped teams define meaningful service level objectives and set up alerts that don't cry wolf.

About the role:

As a Technical Writer at Camunda, you'll be embedded within product teams, taking full ownership of documentation for key areas of our platform. You'll work side-by-side with engineers, product managers, and designers to ensure our documentation is clear, accurate, and closely aligned with the product experience. This is a hands-on role where you'll become a subject matter expert, directly shaping the developer journey through high-impact content across the Camunda platform.

Beyond content, you'll help maintain and configure the infrastructure that keeps our documentation running smoothly. We're looking for someone who can unblock themselves and the team when something breaks. Day to day, this can mean:

  • Troubleshooting and fixing failing GitHub Actions workflows, including reading CI logs, isolating the breaking change, and getting the build green again.

  • Reviewing and merging contributions from engineers and the wider community, and keeping branches and versioned docs releases in good shape.

  • Diagnosing broken links, redirects, MDX and rendering errors, and search indexing issues across current and versioned content.

  • Handling Docusaurus, Node, and dependency upgrades, and resolving the breakages that come with them.

  • Improving the tooling, automation, and linting that writers and contributors rely on, so our publishing process stays fast and predictable

You don't need to be a full-time developer, but you should be confident with Git and GitHub workflows, the command line, YAML and JavaScript-based config, Markdown/MDX, and reading an error trace far enough to know whether you can fix it or need to pull in an engineer.

You'll join a collaborative, mission-driven team focused on helping developers become productive with Camunda technologies quickly and joyfully. Developers with technical writing experience are encouraged to apply.

What You’ll Be Doing:

  1. Own and drive the documentation for one or more product areas, acting as the embedded technical writer within the corresponding product teams.

  2. Maintain and improve our documentation site's technical infrastructure, including build tooling, deployment pipelines, and Docusaurus platform configuration, to keep publishing fast, reliable, and scalable.

  3. Work closely with engineers, product managers, and designers to stay deeply informed about the product roadmap and ensure documentation is accurate, timely, and aligned with feature development.

  4. Become a subject matter expert in your assigned product areas, developing hands-on experience with Camunda products to create documentation that reflects real-world usage and developer needs.

  5. Lead documentation efforts from concept through to release, including planning, writing, reviewing, and maintaining content that empowers developers to succeed with Camunda technologies.

  6. Advocate for documentation as a critical part of the user experience, bringing the user’s perspective into product discussions and influencing design and implementation where appropriate.

  7. Continuously improve the structure, clarity, and completeness of the documentation based on analytics, user feedback, and your own insights.

  8. Collaborate with other writers and the broader Documentation team to share best practices, contribute to team goals, and evolve our documentation tooling and standards.

What You Bring:

  • 3+ years of technical writing experience and a strong portfolio of developer-focused content such as user guides, installation guides, API references, tutorials, and technical blog posts.

  • Proven experience of maintaining, troubleshooting, configuring, and extending documentation site infrastructure and deployment pipelines, preferably using Docusaurus.

  • Hands-on experience with Java, Kubernetes, Helm, Docker, and related technologies, and a proven ability to deeply understand, use, and test complex technical products (ideally with Camunda 8 or similar products).

  • Experience with writing about on-premise software installation or other technical environments, as well as SaaS and software documentation.

  • Proven ability to tailor content for diverse audiences and technical backgrounds, including software engineers, application developers, business analysts, and process owners.

  • Experience with docs-as-code workflows and documentation frameworks such as Docusaurus, and using AI, Git, and Markdown in a developer-centric environment.

  • Ability and/or willingness to use our product.

 Nice-to-haves:

  • Software engineering experience, or proficiency with one or more programming languages.

  • Comfortable iterating on an existing technical writing style guide and advocating for its cross-functional use.

  • Familiarity with orchestration platforms such as Camunda or Clay, and prior work in Revenue Operations, GTM Systems, Sales Operations or Marketing Operations in B2B SaaS.

About the role:

As a Senior Software Engineer on Camunda's new Data Streaming team, you'll help build a foundational new piece of architecture that changes how customers and internal products access process data. Today, customers have no first-class way to stream their own process data out of Camunda, and Camunda's own analytics product is bottlenecked by querying the same storage the live engine depends on. You'll be part of a greenfield team rebuilding how process data is consumed and served at scale, built on top of a durable, continuously-written streaming layer that decouples data consumption from the live engine. You'll be part of a small team from day one, with real room to shape both the architecture and the team's scope as it matures.

At Camunda, we approach engineering in a holistic manner. As such, you will form strong partnerships with product management, the Data Layer and Distributed Systems teams, QA, and support, and work closely with your peers to not only deliver but directly influence how our data streaming architecture evolves to meet our customers' needs.

What You Will Do:

  • Help rebuild how Camunda's analytics product consumes and serves process data at scale, moving it off the engine's critical path entirely.

  • Design and build the core streaming infrastructure that decouples process data access from the live execution engine, backed by durable, object storage.

  • Build customer-facing data streaming capabilities, including a supported way to integrate with systems like Kafka, so customers can reliably get their process data into their own tools.

  • Make foundational architecture decisions as part of a small, high-ownership team, including how the system guarantees consistency and durability across a distributed streaming pipeline.

  • Participate in L3 support and on-call rotations, partnering with Support and SRE to investigate data layer production issues, and feeding what you learn back into the product.

What You Will Bring to the Role:

Must Haves:

  • 7+ years of experience as a backend engineer, in Java, with a strong focus on distributed or data-intensive systems.

  • Hands-on experience building or operating an analytical serving layer over a table format such as Apache Iceberg or Delta Lake - including experience with an embedded/lightweight query engine (e.g. DuckDB, or similar), or a stateful stream-processing framework (e.g. Flink, Kafka Streams).

  • A track record of working with object storage systems (S3/GCS/Azure or similar) and building reliable, idempotent upload/commit protocols against them.

  • Solid grounding in the reasoning behind correctness and consistency in data-intensive systems (e.g. concurrent writes, atomicity, idempotency).

  • A demonstrated track record of driving a technical initiative through genuine ambiguity in a still-being-designed system, not just extending an established one.

  • Proven experience leading medium-to-large engineering initiatives (3+ months) end-to-end, from solution design, project planning, and coordinating across teams, right through to driving predictable delivery.

  • Strong communication and collaboration skills in a remote-first environment: you translate requirements into actionable technical work with Product, and give and receive clear, direct feedback in code review.

Nice to Haves:

  • Experience with Kafka or a similar streaming/event-log system

  • Experience with embedded state stores (RocksDB or similar) for projection/checkpointing workloads.

  • Experience with stream processing frameworks (e.g. Apache Flink), particularly stateful processing with local state backends and checkpointing.

  • Familiarity with object-storage-native streaming architectures (e.g. systems like WarpStream) is a plus, even without direct hands-on experience.

Visionary in 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. ranked 3rd in Flexa's 2026 Most Flexible Companies, We’re growing fast and looking for top talent to join our team. If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading.

About the role:

We're hiring for Self-Managed Experience (SMX) — the team responsible for making Camunda 8 deployable in a self-service way for customers who run their own infrastructure. SMX covers two areas of work: installation artifacts (Helm chart, Docker Compose, C8Run) and reference architectures & cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, Azure).

This role sits primarily on the installation artifacts side — building, maintaining, and releasing the artifacts that ship Camunda 8 to every self-managed customer. You'll be fully embedded in that area day-to-day, but you'll work alongside the reference-architecture side of the team regularly, and SMX is actively working toward enabling every engineer to review and contribute across both stacks over time.

SMX is also shifting from a purely artifact- and ops-focused team toward one in which engineers bring customer judgment and product sense alongside technical depth. That means engaging directly with the teams closest to customers — Support, Consulting, Presales — and using that signal to help shape what we prioritize, not just executing a fully-specced ticket.

You'll find plenty of room to leave your own footprint: deployment automation, software and infrastructure testing, multi-region setups, and developer experience are all live areas of investment as the team matures from "basic install" toward full-lifecycle ownership (upgrades, backup/restore, disaster recovery).

Curious about the kind of challenges you'll work on at Camunda? Watch this quick 30-minute talk from our engineers to learn more about the new Camunda Exporter and how we’re solving complex problems at scale

What You’ll Be Doing:

  •  Build, maintain, and release C8 distribution artifacts for self-managed customers — Helm Charts (Kubernetes), C8Run, and Docker Compose — along with their documentation.

  • Improve the reliability and usability of deployment artifacts across the full customer lifecycle: installation, upgrades, and day-2 operations, not just initial deployment.

  • Engage directly with internal customer-facing teams (Support, Consulting, Presales) to understand real deployment problems, and use that signal to help shape what gets prioritized — not just how it gets built. Collaborate with Development Teams, Product Management, QA, and Documentation to ship integrated, tested, and documented releases.

  • Take part in the team's shared medic rotation and resolve engineering-level support cases, feeding learnings back into development.

  • Contribute to the shared tooling (review, deployment, and test tooling) that SMX is building so other Camunda teams can adopt it — this is one of the team's current investment areas.

What success looks like (first ~3 months):

  • Taken on your first medic rotation slot and support tickets to understand the stack, customer challenges, and deployment environments.

  • Improved onboarding or documentation, turning your own ramp-up experience into concrete improvements.

  • Contributed to artifact fixes, CI/CD enhancements, or test automation that strengthens release quality.

  • Deliver structural improvement initiatives — a feature request, or a test/release improvement.

  • Built working relationships with engineering, QA, and product peers, and started building context on the reference-architecture side of the team.

  • Started forming your own view of a customer pain point from firsthand signal (support tickets, consulting feedback), not just from a ticket description.

What You Bring:

  • Ability and/or willingness to use our product, with genuine curiosity about the customer problem behind a ticket — comfortable asking "should we build this" as well as "how do we build this."

  • Strong expertise in building, operating, and maintaining Helm Charts; deploying applications on Kubernetes; implementing CI/CD pipelines with GitHub Actions; and managing infrastructure as code (e.g., Terraform).

  • Ability to create clear technical documentation and communicate effectively across teams.

  • A pragmatic and autonomous approach to programming and problem-solving.

  • You thrive as a manager of one — you build it, you own it — and take pride in delivering maintainable, operable software.

 Nice-to-haves:

  • Experience running and operating on-prem/self-hosted software on Docker.

  • Familiarity with Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or similar observability tools.

  • Working knowledge of the Go programming language.

  • Exposure to cloud infrastructure/IaC (Terraform, Crossplane) — useful as SMX moves toward shared review capability across installation artifacts and reference architectures.

About the role:

As a Backend Software Engineer on the Data Layer team, you'll help build and evolve the storage and query layer that keeps Camunda 8's process data fast, accurate, and available at scale. Spanning both relational databases and Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, the data layer and its data pipelines power everything from process monitoring to the new agent-driven automation capabilities we're rolling out.

As part of the Data Layer team, you will work on both technically challenging and rewarding projects, such as reshaping how we store and retain process data, streaming data to external systems, and evolving our secondary storage systems to perform at ever greater scale.

At Camunda, we approach engineering in a holistic manner. As such, you will form strong partnerships with product management, design, QA, and support, and work with your peers to not only deliver but directly influence how our data layer evolves to meet our customers' needs.

Curious about the kind of challenges you'll work on at Camunda? Watch this quick 30-minute talk from our engineers to learn more about the new Camunda Exporter and how we’re solving complex problems at scale.

What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Design, build, and maintain backend services for the data layer that stores and serves Camunda 8's process data, spanning relational databases and Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, with an eye toward correctness, performance, and scale.

  • Own the end-to-end delivery of engineering initiatives, working with Product Management and senior colleagues to break down requirements into concrete solution designs, driving projects to timely and high-quality delivery.

  • Help evolve how we process, retain, and expose process data, so customers can work with their data the way they need to.

  • Invest in making our secondary storage systems more performant and scalable as usage grows, and build tooling that makes it easier to understand, troubleshoot, and safely operate the data layer in production.

  • Participate in L3 support and on-call rotations, partnering with Support and SRE to investigate data layer production issues, and feeding what you learn back into the product.

What You Will Bring to the Role:

Must Haves:

  • At least 4 years of experience as a backend engineer, with a strong focus on backend systems and production data stores

  • Hands-on experience with at least one of PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MSSQL, or Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, with a practical understanding of query performance, indexing, and data modeling trade-offs

  • Experience contributing to complex engineering initiatives: breaking down requirements into concrete tasks, writing clear technical designs for your piece of the work, and delivering reliably

  • Comfortable investigating slow queries, execution plans, and index usage to root-cause data-related production issues.

  • Strong communication and collaboration skills in a remote-first environment: you translate requirements into actionable technical work with Product, and give and receive clear, direct feedback in code review.

Nice to Haves:

  • Experience building workflow automation or process orchestration software.

  • Experience working with both relational databases and Elasticsearch/OpenSearch.

  • Experience building or maintaining CI pipelines.

  • Understanding of database migration tooling (e.g. Liquibase, Flyway) and schema evolution in a live system.

Sardine is the leading agentic risk platform for fighting financial crime. Our integrated solution unifies data across risk teams to help organizations stop fraud in real time, prevent AI-driven attacks, and automate fraud and AML operations. Sardine’s platform is strengthened by one of the fastest-growing fraud consortiums in the market, spanning more than 6 billion profiled devices, 800 million consumers, and 3 million businesses worldwide. Leading companies including FIS, GoDaddy, Intuit, Edward Jones, ZoomInfo, and Checkout.com rely on Sardine to secure and grow trust in their products.

Our culture:

  • We hire talented, self-motivated individuals with extreme ownership and high growth orientation.

  • We value performance and not hours worked. We believe you shouldn't have to miss your family dinner, your kid's school play, friends get-together, or doctor's appointments for the sake of adhering to an arbitrary work schedule.

  • From Home / Beach / Mountain / Cafe / Anywhere!

About the role:

Sales Engineering is a team of subject matter experts who serve as the trusted technical advisor to prospective customers. You will lead prospects through the sales process by connecting their needs to Sardine’s value to win new customers and drive revenue growth. You will deliver best in class product demonstrations, fill out RFPs, and win over our prospective customer’s technical teams with your thought leadership and consultative approach. Internally, your insights from the field will help shape our product roadmap and will pave the way for future customers. You will play a key role in our commitment to customer excellence and allow Sardine to stay ahead of market trends.

The SE team is a high visibility and high impact team. At the intersection of our Go-To-Market and Product and Engineering teams, we serve as the link between our customer’s needs and the Sardine’s capabilities, ensuring our platform is always adding value to our customer’s Fraud and Compliance stack. It's a great role for someone who enjoys learning the intricacies of a product to drive value to prospects, and leading through innovative problem-solving to convert prospects into customers. Variety, ambiguity, innovation, and ownership of complex problems are all big components of this role.


What you'll be doing:

  • Support Account Executives in identifying a prospect’s fraud and compliance needs.

  • Prepare and deliver customized demos that showcase the impact of Sardine’s platform.

  • Interface with Security teams to articulate our security posture and successfully complete security reviews.

  • Complete RFPs for competitive opportunities.

  • Create comprehensive Solution Designs that address our prospect’s needs.

  • Collaborate with peers to improve all processes within the Sales Engineering team.

  • Work together with our product and engineering teams to identify areas for improvement in our product suite and help prioritize and design solutions.

 

What you’ll need:

  • 7+ years prior experience as a Sales Engineer, System Engineer, Solutions Engineer, or similar roles

  • Prior experience in similar roles within the Risk, Fraud, or Compliance domain

  • Experience with APIs, a strong understanding of JSON, and proficiency in one or more of the following languages: Python, JavaScript, Ruby, Go, or Java. Bonus points for knowledge of web development principles and/or the ability to build internal tools using one of these languages.

  • Strong analytical skills: you can dig into the technical details of a problem and turn it into a proposed solution

  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced remote environment working with global clients

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex technical and business concepts to technical and non-technical personas.

jobs.title: MSF Access 101 Project - Consultation Design Consultant
jobs.description:
Title of the function: MSF Access 101 Project - Consultation Design Consultant

Contract: Consultancy - The candidate must have rights to work as a “Consultant” in their country of residence

Duration: Approximately 20-25 working days between October 2026 to January 2027

Location: Home based

Deadline to apply: October 06, 2026

Reports to: MSF Access Internal Communications Officer

I. MSF INTERNATIONAL

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF assists people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation.
MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 24 sections, 27 associations and 18 branch offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested.

 

II. BACKGROUND

MSF Access 

Médecins Sans Frontières works tirelessly to improve the accessibility, availability, affordability, appropriateness and quality of health products for the populations it assists and their communities. While this is a shared responsibility across the organisation, the MSF Access team plays a central role in driving and supporting MSF's work to improve access to health products.

Rooted in MSF's medical humanitarian mission, MSF Access works to identify and address barriers that prevent people from obtaining the medicines, diagnostics, vaccines and other health products they need. The team coordinates access-related priorities, provides expertise and support across the MSF Movement, and monitors developments in the global access landscape to inform MSF's strategies and actions.

MSF Access operates through five regional hubs in Brussels, Belgium; Dakar, Senegal; Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia; Nairobi, Kenya; and Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

The team's work is currently guided by seven Common Priorities agreed by the MSF Movement: Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR), Cancer, Diabetes, Diagnostic Tools, Sexual and Reproductive Health, Tuberculosis, and Vaccines.

 

Access 101 Project

Access 101 is a new learning initiative led by MSF Access that aims to strengthen the understanding of access to health products across the MSF Movement. In 2023, MSF adopted its first collective vision for improving access to products for healthcare, recognizing this work as an essential part of delivering on MSF's social mission and a shared responsibility across the MSF Movement. To realize this ambition and leverage MSF's collective strength in this area, colleagues across MSF need a common understanding of what "access" means, why it matters, and how they can contribute to improving access to health products for the people who are deprived of them.

The Access 101 project will develop a range of learning resources, including an introductory course on Tembo (MSF’s e-learning platform), supporting educational materials, and regional workshops. These resources will help MSF staff better understand the global access landscape, MSF's approach to improving access, and the role they can play in identifying and addressing access barriers.

The project begins with a consultation phase to identify access-related knowledge gaps, learning needs, interests, and preferences among diverse audiences across MSF. Insights from this consultation will inform the design of the access Tembo course curriculum and ensure that the learning experience is relevant, engaging, and accessible to colleagues in diverse roles and locations.

The project receives funding from the MSF Access Fund. The Fund was created by the MSF International Board in 2023 to amplify the capacity of MSF Access, Sections, and Operational Directorates to respond to the access opportunities or address emerging threats.

 

III.    PURPOSE

The Consultation Design Consultant will lead the design and implementation of a consultation process to identify access-related learning needs, knowledge gaps, interests and preferences across the MSF Movement. Using insights gathered through qualitative and quantitative research, the consultant will develop recommendations for the syllabus for the Access 101 Tembo course and the focus and scope of supporting learning materials and regional workshops that complement the course.

 

IV.    MAIN ACTIVITIES

Consultation design and implementation

  • Develop a consultation methodology and work-plan to identify learning needs, knowledge gaps, interests and preferences related to access to health products across MSF.

  • Design and implement a mixed-methods consultation process, combining qualitative and quantitative approaches as appropriate.

  • Prepare consultation tools and materials, including interview guides, survey questionnaires, and data collection frameworks.

  • Conduct interviews, focus groups and/or other consultation activities with a diverse range of stakeholders across regions, operational entities and functions within MSF.

  • Ensure the consultation process reflects diversity, equity and inclusion principles and captures perspectives from different regions, roles and levels of the organisation.

Analysis and recommendations

  • Analyse consultation findings and identify key learning needs, knowledge gaps, barriers, motivations and audience preferences relevant to access-related learning.

  • Produce a report summarising findings and providing practical recommendations to inform the design of Access 101 learning products and activities.

  • Present findings and recommendations to the Access 101 project team and relevant stakeholders.

Course syllabus development

  • Translate consultation findings into recommendations for a syllabus for the Access 101 Tembo course.

  • Recommend learning objectives, thematic areas, audience segmentation, and priority content modules.

  • Advise on suitable learning formats and approaches, including the balance between e-learning, downloadable resources and regional workshops.

 

V.      DELIVERABLES

  •  Consultation methodology, work-plan and stakeholder engagement approach

  • Survey and interview/focus group tools

  • Consultation findings report, including analysis of what meaningful engagement between MSF Access and MSF operations looks like, and recommendations

  • Presentation of findings to the project team.

  • Recommendations for the Access 101 course syllabus and workshop approach


  • A degree in Education, Social Sciences, Public Health, Organizational Development, or a related field.

  • Minimum 3 years of experience in learning design, curriculum development, organizational learning, or stakeholder consultation.

  • Demonstrated experience designing and implementing qualitative and quantitative consultation or research processes.

  • Strong analytical and report-writing skills.

  • Experience engaging diverse stakeholders across regions, functions, and cultural contexts.

  • Excellent written and spoken English; knowledge of French, Spanish, Arabic, or Portuguese is an asset.

jobs.title: Deployment Lead - ERP Solutions
jobs.description:
What We Do

Rillet serves accounting and finance teams, the financial brains of their companies. Our job is to help them run the numbers with impossible speed, accuracy, and insight.

Rillet is the Agentic ERP built for modern finance teams. We help companies automate the most critical parts of finance, from closing the books and recognizing revenue to consolidating entities and reporting to investors. More than 600 companies run on Rillet, including Mercor, Scribe, and Function Health, and we partner with leading accounting firms including EY and KPMG.

We’re building in one of the largest software markets in the world, with the momentum to match. Rillet has raised more than $200M, is valued at $1B, and is backed by Sequoia, a16z, ICONIQ, Bain Capital Ventures, Oak HC/FT, and other leading investors. We’re using that backing to build the financial infrastructure for the next generation of companies and help every business run its numbers at the speed of AI.

Who We Are

Rillet’s pace is not for everyone. Intelligence is table stakes. To succeed here, you need extreme speed, agency, and flexibility.

The people who thrive at Rillet do not wait for assignments. They internalize the mission, design a strategy, and bring back results that are better, faster, and more creative than a manager could have asked for.

Our work revolves around our customers. The people who succeed here are energized by delivering what matters most, even when it was not part of the original plan.

Rillet is built on deep accounting expertise, and it takes people from many disciplines to build a category-defining company. You do not need to be an accountant to thrive here. You do need to care deeply about the problems we solve and the impact our customers can create. Together, we combine the precision of accounting with the speed, creativity, and ambition of AI-native software to power the financial core of the world’s fastest-growing companies while redefining what finance teams should expect from their software.

Who We Need

We are building industry-defining accounting and finance software. We are looking for an experienced Deployment Lead to guide complex customer implementations and help finance teams successfully transition onto Rillet.

This role is ideal for someone who has led ERP implementations and understands how to turn complex accounting and operational requirements into practical systems solutions. You may come from an ERP implementation firm, Big 4 finance transformation practice, systems consulting team, or a SaaS company serving finance organizations. You are comfortable owning multiple workstreams, advising senior stakeholders, and navigating the details of configuration, data migration, integrations, testing, and go-live.

You will combine strong implementation judgment with a customer-first mindset—bringing structure to ambiguity, identifying risks early, and keeping customers and internal teams moving toward a successful launch.

We’re primarily looking for teammates who are based near our New York City or San Francisco offices, or open to relocating. For this role, we’re also open to remote candidates based anywhere in the United States. Our hybrid schedule brings office-based team members together in person on Tuesdays and Thursdays, plus one additional flexible day each week. Some roles may spend more time in the office depending on the needs of the team.

What You'll Do

  • Lead key parts of customer onboarding and deployment, helping ensure a smooth and timely implementation experience

  • Partner with internal teams across Product, Engineering, and Customer Success to execute implementation plans and solve customer problems quickly

  • Learn and analyze client accounting and finance workflows, then translate those needs into clear requirements and practical solutions

  • Guide customers through onboarding, training, change management, and adoption

  • Support data migration, reconciliations, systems setup, and integration coordination

  • Track milestones, drive follow-through, and keep internal and external stakeholders aligned throughout the onboarding process

  • Identify risks early, escalate issues quickly, and help keep customer launches on track

  • Build trust with customers by being responsive, thoughtful, and solutions-oriented

  • Maintain clear documentation and provide regular status updates to customers and internal stakeholders

Who We're Looking For

  • 4–7 years in ERP implementation, systems consulting, or finance transformation (e.g., Big 4 or implementation firms)

  • Background in SaaS, high-growth technology companies, or implementation/consulting environments is strongly preferred

  • Hands-on ERP experience (NetSuite, SAP, Workday, etc.), including requirements, configuration, data migration, and go-live

  • Strong understanding of core accounting workflows (close, reconciliations, ASC 606) and how they translate into systems

  • Customer-facing with strong communication and stakeholder management skills

  • Systems-minded with solid project management skills; able to run multiple workstreams

  • Comfortable in fast-paced, ambiguous environments and highly detail-oriented

  • Experience working cross-functionally with technical and non-technical teams

The expected base salary range for this role varies by location:

Tier A: $100,000 – $150,000
Tier B: $100,000 – $140,000
Tier C: $100,000 – $130,000

Your compensation tier is based on your primary work location. You can view Rillet’s compensation zones here.

Final compensation within the applicable range will depend on factors including skills, experience, qualifications, and the scope of the role. This role is also eligible for equity and benefits.

 

Note: All official Rillet recruiting communications will come from an @rillet.com email address. If you’re contacted from another domain, please disregard the message and report it as spam.

Life at Rillet

  • Grow with us. Take meaningful ownership, expand your scope, and make an impact as Rillet scales.

  • Competitive pay and meaningful equity. Be rewarded for the value you help create.

  • Benefits that support you. We offer competitive benefits designed to support your health, wellbeing, time away from work, family, and long-term financial goals.

  • Better together. We value collaboration, connection, and spending meaningful time together as a team. We regularly create opportunities to connect through team meals, events, and company gatherings.

Compensation: $100K – $150K • Offers Equity • Multiple Ranges

  • Zone A • $100K – $150K • Offers Equity
  • Zone B • $100K – $140K • Offers Equity
  • Zone C • $100K – $130K • Offers Equity

About Fyxer

Fyxer launched in May 2024 and hit $1M in revenue across 3,000 paid users without spending a dollar on marketing. We've since gone from $1M to $30M ARR and raised a Series B led by Madrona, with Lakestar, 20VC and Marc Benioff behind us.

Far more people start using Fyxer every month than we can speak to. Nobody owns turning those users into paying teams. That's the biggest surface in the company, and it's this seat.

The role

You work accounts where someone is already using the product. One person trying Fyxer is often a door into a 500-person company. Spot those fast, get to the people who sign, prove out the pattern so it repeats.

You run the full cycle. First touch, discovery, demo, pricing, close. No handoffs.

You also write the first version of everything: the pitch, the sequences, the objection handling, the qualification bar. None of it exists yet. What you prove out is what the next reps get trained on.

  • High performer, president club pedigree seller who can name 30+ deals you closed yourself in the last 12 months

Three years in or twelve. We care what you've done, not where you did it.

How we work

Time with customers is the only thing that compounds. Everything else is overhead. We automate the research, the notes, the CRM and the follow-up with our own product.

  • Respect and support others

If you are passionate about mobile app development and want to join a company that’s reshaping the industry, Gismart is the place for you. About project


At Radiotech, we believe music belongs to everyone — not just those who grew up taking lessons. As a product company inside the Gismart ecosystem, we’ve spent years building apps that make music feel approachable, fun, and deeply human. With 23 apps across iOS and Android and over 500 million downloads worldwide, our products have found their way into the hands of musicians, beginners, and curious souls across the globe. We see music as a universal language. Our job is to make sure more people can speak it.

The Creative Production Lead owns the strategic growth of the creative production function, translating company-level goals into team execution while building the people, processes, and cross-functional relationships needed to scale creative output. This role is a defined growth track toward Head of Creative Production, with scope expanding as the team and its impact on business metrics grow.

Responsibilities:

1. Strategy & Performance

  • Decompose company OKRs into actionable creative team goals and KPIs

  • Track OKR completion, creative output volume, and performance against targets

  • Report on team performance and creative impact to leadership

2. People Management

  • Full ownership of team management: hiring, onboarding, and performance reviews

  • Design and run career development paths, including promotion criteria

  • Build a team education program (skills growth, internal training, external learning)

  • Manage team capacity planning and workload distribution

3. Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Build and maintain strong working relationships with Product, PMM, and UA teams

  • Align creative priorities with product roadmaps and UA testing needs

  • Represent creative production in cross-functional planning cycles

4. Process & Automation

  • Identify and drive automation opportunities across the creative production pipeline (briefing, asset delivery, QA, reporting)

  • Own tooling decisions and process documentation

  • Continuously reduce time-to-launch for creative assets

5. Team Culture & Knowledge Sharing

  • Establish and run team rituals (standups, retros, creative reviews)

  • Drive in-house knowledge sharing (playbooks, best-practice libraries, post-mortems)

  • Foster a culture of experimentation and continuous improvement

Experience:

  • 4+ years in creative production, creative strategy, or performance creative roles, with at least 1-2 years in a team lead or management capacity

  • Proven track record producing creative for performance marketing channels (Meta, AppLovin, TikTok, or similar)

  • Experience with mobile app or gaming creative production is a strong plus; familiarity with playable ads (e.g. Cocos Creator or similar engines) is a bonus

  • Experience managing creative production budgets and resourcing (in-house team, freelancers, or agencies)

Mindset:

  • Systems thinker — genuinely energized by building process and automation, not just managing output

  • Growth-oriented, with clear interest in scaling into a Head of Creative Production role

  • Comfortable operating in a fast-paced, iteration-heavy environment (multiple products, frequent creative testing cycles)

Employee Benefits:

  • Remote-First Culture: Our team is diverse and extensive, just like our product portfolio. We provide a flexible working schedule and let you work anywhere in the world, either remotely or in one of our corporate hubs

  • Public Holidays Policy: Gismart observes public holidays based on the Ukrainian or Polish holiday calendars. Employees working in other locations are entitled to 12 public holidays per year

  • Corporate Events: We are remote-first, but we love meeting up in person. Whenever possible, we organize corporate events and team-building activities across all Gismart hubs

jobs.title: Endear - Product Designer
jobs.description:
Location: Remote, US-based
Team: Product & Design — IRL
Type: Full-Time, Employee
Compensation: $100K–$129K base
Target Start: January 2027 or earlier

Our Story

At Endear, we’re building the modern CRM for retail teams — starting with the frontline.

Our software helps retail teams build stronger customer relationships through thoughtful, intuitive technology. From clienteling and customer capture to appointments and in-store experiences, Endear gives brands the tools they need to create more personal interactions and drive measurable growth.

We work with brands like Allbirds, Reformation, and Alo Yoga, and we’re continuing to evolve Endear into an increasingly AI-first product built around how modern retail teams actually work.

Position Overview

We’re looking for a Product Designer to join our IRL (in real life) team, which owns the in-store side of Endear — including appointments, events, customer check-ins, and the administrative experiences behind those workflows.

You’ll design for store associates and managers running clienteling day to day, as well as admin users who help shape how those teams operate and manage their workflows.

In this role, you’ll own features and projects from understanding the problem through research, testing, iteration, and production-ready design, while partnering closely with our Head of Product Design on vision and direction.

The IRL roadmap is early. Many of these features don’t exist yet, so you’ll be defining problems through research before designing solutions.

This role is well suited for someone comfortable creating clarity when the solution isn’t obvious.

What You’ll Accomplish

In your first 6 months, you’ll…

  • Take ownership of IRL features from discovery through production-ready design

  • Build a strong understanding of how store associates, managers, and admin users work within Endear

  • Run research from early discovery through usability testing

  • Design complete, accessible product experiences, including loading, empty, error, permission, and other key states.

  • Partner closely with Product and Engineering to shape solutions early in the process

  • Use customer insight and data to inform design decisions and iteration

In your first year, you’ll…

  • Build deeper ownership across the IRL product

  • Deliver product experiences that improve how retail teams manage clienteling and in-store workflows

  • Build a strong rhythm of discovery, testing, and continuous learning

  • Strengthen your collaboration across Design, Product, and Engineering

  • Demonstrate clear user and business impact through the work you ship

You’ll Thrive in This Role If…

  • You enjoy taking ownership of a feature while collaborating closely on the broader vision and direction

  • You’re comfortable with ambiguity and zero-to-one product work

  • You naturally think beyond the happy path and account for edge cases and complete product states

  • You care about creating accessible experiences and solving the right problem, not just creating polished UI

  • You enjoy working closely with Product and Engineering throughout the design process

  • You’re comfortable using research, data, and customer feedback to guide decisions

  • You move quickly, seek feedback, and iterate based on what you learn

  • You’re curious about designing for AI

You Have Experience With

  • 2–5 years working in product design

  • Independently owning features from discovery through implementation, with support on vision and direction

  • Running user research from discovery through usability testing

  • Translating broad or ambiguous problems into clear product solutions

  • Working closely with Design, Product, and Engineering teams

  • Designing complex, accessible workflows and accounting for loading, empty, error, and permission states

  • Using qualitative and quantitative data to inform design decisions

  • Building within established design patterns while knowing when something needs to evolve

  • Using AI tools as part of your workflow and applying judgment to AI-generated output

  • A portfolio that demonstrates strong product thinking and execution, and where you can articulate the impact of your work, with data where you had access to it

Align With What We Value

At Endear, we live by five core principles. Here’s how they translate into what we’re looking for in this role:

  • Customer First: You start by understanding the people using the product, run thoughtful research, and use what you learn to shape better experiences.

  • Take Ownership: You take responsibility for your features, follow through on the details, and care about the quality of what ships.

  • Enable Autonomy: You communicate clearly, collaborate early, and give Product and Engineering the context they need to make strong decisions together.

  • Under Promise, Over Deliver: You set realistic expectations, think through the details, and deliver complete, production-ready work.

  • Innovate & Deliver Value Quickly: You’re comfortable experimenting, using AI and other tools thoughtfully, and moving quickly without sacrificing sound product judgment.

About the Team

Endear’s product organization is structured across three product teams: AI, IRL, and Core Flows, with one designer dedicated to each.

As the IRL designer, you’ll work closely with a Product Manager and 2–3 Engineers while also being part of Endear’s three-person design team. You’ll report to the Head of Product Design, who will provide vision, direction, mentorship, and support as you grow in the role.

You’ll partner most closely with:

  • Head of Product Design: vision, direction, mentorship, feedback, and design leadership

  • Product Team: roadmap alignment, priorities, customer needs, and business context

  • Engineering Team: feasibility, implementation, and iteration

You’ll have access to mentorship, an education budget, and support around Endear’s AI processes to help you continue developing your craft and expanding how you use AI in your work.

We’re a small team with big ambitions — collaborative, customer-obsessed, and deeply excited about the problems we’re solving in retail.

Our Hiring Process

  1. Recruiter Screen

  2. Behavioral Interview with the Hiring Manager

  3. Team Portfolio Review with Design, Product + Engineering

  4. Final leadership conversation

  5. Offer 🎉

Compensation & Benefits

  • Base Salary: $100K–$129K

  • Fully remote, US-based team

  • Comprehensive healthcare (medical, dental, vision)

  • Co-working or home office stipend

  • Flexible PTO and unlimited vacation

  • Education and learning support

  • Opportunity to shape foundational product work in a transformative industry

Location: This role is remote and US-based. Our full team comes together for an all-team standup every Monday at 8:00 AM Pacific, so you’ll need to be available at that time.

Apply Even If You Don’t Check Every Box

If this role excites you but you’re unsure if you meet every requirement, reach out anyway. No retail or e-commerce background is required. We care about your product thinking, skills, motivation, and how you approach problems more than we do about perfect resumes.

jobs.title: Knit - Research Manager
jobs.description:
Knit is the AI-native consumer research platform helping brands automate and accelerate primary research. With our Researcher-Driven AI, we’ve condensed the entire quant + qual research process from weeks into days (sometimes hours!) for 50+ enterprise brands — including Amazon, T-Mobile, Mars, NASCAR, and more. We’re on a mission to scale and democratize world-class research. From survey generation to stakeholder-ready reports, our platform is redefining how insights teams operate — and we need your help to push the limits of what’s possible.


Overview

The purpose of the Research Manager role is to ensure Knit customers successfully achieve their desired research outcomes through their partnerships with Knit. By owning and supporting customer relationships, getting deeply engrained in customer research needs, and driving high-quality project deliverables, the Research Manager’s impact is ultimately measured by positive customer retention.

Responsibilities:

The research function is a primary contributor to Knit’s shared business objectives of customer retention and upsells, ultimately measured by Net Revenue Retention (NRR) in addition to supporting successful Pilot to Subscription Conversions for acquiring new business.

The levers the Research Manager role owns to influence these key business objectives are:

  • Research Success → Ensuring Knit Customers successfully achieve their desired research outcomes through their projects with Knit, measured by successfully achieving Research Objectives and delivering on Knit’s Quality & Speed service-level agreements (SLA’s)

Primary responsibilities of this role:

  • Serving as the dedicated research lead for all customers’ projects (on assigned accounts) and serving as the ultimate accountable part for research project success

  • Driving and documenting in-depth project scoping to uncover a deep understanding of research objectives and project context to set up project success

  • Demonstrate a growth mindset as a solutions architect for customers, educating them on Knit’s research capabilities, consulting with them to adjust for fringe requirements, and proposing solutions to maximize project success - escalating to Research Directors when needs exceed capabilities

  • Escalating needs to Research Directors to support troubleshooting when increased risk for project viability or customer impact occurs

  • Driving, maintaining, and enriching all customer context to improve Knit’s ability to meet the customers’ custom research needs

  • Being the final, customer-ready check and approver on all Knit final topline delivery and presenting the key insights and recommendations directly to the customers

  • Participating in continuous innovation on Knit’s AI product to minimize the delta between Knit’s AI output and a human researcher output

  • Driving on feedback collection on “the last mile” - uncovering and documenting what happens after Knit delivers a project to when it’s “stakeholder ready,” supporting Knit’s product vision in getting to stakeholder ready reports

Required Skills & Experiences:

  • Must have 5+ years of market research experience, with the majority of the time spent on the supplier side in a market research agency environment.

  • Must have experience leading discovery and scoping calls, writing and editing quant and qual questionnaires from scratch, drafting analysis plans, and creating and presenting stakeholder-ready insights topline & reports.

  • Ability to drive initiatives and outcomes in ambiguous environments, both for navigating complex customer needs and Knit internal business changes. Proven track record successfully operating in an early stage startup (<50 employees) is a plus.

  • Proven track record of owning and supporting client relationships with customers at Enterprise, Fortune 500 US-based companies, specifically working with insights professionals to scope and achieve desired research outcomes, resulting in customer retention and growth.

  • Ability to drive initiatives and outcomes successfully in environments with competing priorities, multiple research projects on at a given time, and simultaneous internal business demands.

Benefits

Upon joining the Knit team, you will receive a competitive salary + commission plan if applicable to role, Equity Options, Healthcare (medical, dental, and vision), and Additional Coverage, a company laptop and one-time, onboarding Technology Stipend, a 401(k) with company match, flexible time-off, hybrid working, and more!

Salary

In accordance with New York pay transparency requirements, the salary range for this role is $115,000 - $130,000. Final compensation will be determined based on the candidate’s level, experience, and qualifications upon joining Knit.

Our Company Values

We are the Championship Team. This means we:

  • Are 1% better every day: We approach situations with a growth mindset and ask, “How can we make the business better?” and “What would it take?”

  • Play to win: We set audacious goals and push ourselves to achieve them with a bias towards action (When we see a need, we take initiative, and hold ourselves accountable to seeing it through).

  • Keep the main thing the main thing: Identify what has the biggest impact and prioritize to focus on it.

The role

  • Customer workshops, discovery, and requirements (35%). Run technical discovery and workshops with each client, and translate their needs into clear, buildable product requirements for our sales, ops, and engineering teams. Flag what we need to build to support a given setup, such as client self-hosting.

  • Procurement, security, and delivery oversight (30%). Use our existing compliance library (SOC 2 program, DPAs, prior questionnaire answers) to complete security questionnaires, handle security committees and data-residency questions, and drive procurement to completion. Oversee the MCP deployment itself, which our freelancer network implements.

Across all three, you build the reusable kit that makes this repeatable: scoping templates, architecture patterns, and a procurement answer library.

Objectives

  • 90 days: own scoping and procurement response for active deals, with the reusable kit used on at least one live deal end to end.

  • You are technically credible: you read code, reason fluently about integrations and the MCP and agent stack, and can scope and oversee a deployment. This is not a hands-on production-coding role; implementation is handled by our freelancer network.

What this role is not

  • A backend engineering role. You will work with clients most of the week.

jobs.title: Lead Product Manager - RPG
jobs.description:
Homa is a global mobile game developer and publisher creating games people love. We partner with studios and internally develop games, having launched over 80 titles, reached over 2 billion downloads, and seen our game All in Hole break into the global top-50 grossing charts. These are milestones, not the finish line. 

With deep expertise in product and technology, we built Homa Lab, our proprietary platform that gives developers the market intelligence, data tools, and game tech, with AI built-in, to find product–market fit fast and scale mass-market games into lasting experiences players enjoy for years.

This is our flywheel: Homa Lab helps studios spot the right ideas early, turn them into games quickly, and reach millions of players. Every launch brings back data and insights that fuel the next hit, making each turn of the loop faster, smarter, and more likely to win. AI supercharges this process, running through everything we do, from everyday tasks to our guiding principles.

What powers the loop is talent density. 220+ people from 30+ nationalities, bringing expertise from the world’s best studios and companies. We uphold ambition, curiosity, humility, and focus, and deliver with speed, excellence, and candor. Since the start, we’ve raised $165M from Headline, Northzone, Eurazeo, Bpifrance, and the founders of King, Sorare, and Spotify, people who’ve built and backed the games and platforms we admire, now supporting our drive to create the next ones.

At Homa, we are building the next billion-player experiences from the ground up and shaping the future of entertainment.

Mission

As a Lead Product Manager on our RPG games, you'll play a key role in defining and owning the product roadmap for our live RPG games portfolio end-to-end, starting by turning one of our current strongest live titles into a franchise players stay with for years. You'll start with one game, and as our RPG portfolio expands, so does your scope, more titles, and a real hand in the product strategy behind them. You're shaping how Homa runs RPG as a whole.

Your main responsibilities will include:

  • Define the product roadmap across one or more live RPG titles: core loop, progression pacing, monetization, and meta systems such as gacha, PvP, seasons, and guild or pass structures, with the health of the in-game economy.
  • Own LiveOps end-to-end. You'll define the calendar, the events, and the loop that brings players back by a real understanding of what the team can design, produce, and sustain sprint over sprint: ambitious, but grounded.
  • Lead your team. You'll have a talented but small team of product, design, and economy experts to lead towards the same goal. Your job is to give them a clear plan, raise their level, and get the best out of them.
  • Oversee the monetization model. Working closely with economy, you're accountable for leading how the game balances the IAP and ad revenue growth together rather than at each other's expense.
  • Drive growth, in partnership with UA. You're responsible for how the game scales on the acquisition side: working hand-in-hand with the UA team so that the player data, creative learnings, and campaign performance shapes the product roadmap.
  • Cross-functional excellence. You'll work hand-in-hand with Publishing and the studios, through logic and shared KPIs, which means understanding how a game gets built and shipped end-to-end, from concept to launch.
  • Set the bar. Bring genre benchmarks and proven best practices into every major call, so the team always has a clear, shared sense of what great looks like in this genre.
  • Stay hands-on when it counts. This is a leadership role, but you'll stay close enough to the data and the systems to go deep personally on whatever matters most that month, rather than directing only from a distance.

This is a great opportunity to take a genuinely exceptional game and decide what it becomes: full ownership of the product, the economy, and the LiveOps of a title Homa is betting on, real autonomy over how you get there, and a clear path to leading product across our whole RPG portfolio as it grows.

Requirements

We are looking for someone with several years of product experience on live mobile games, especially RPG, with genuine end-to-end ownership of an economy, progression system or monetization roadmap, and the humility, curiosity, ambition, and drive to make an impact fast. You're a great fit if you have:

Product & RPG expertise

  • Product experience on live F2P mobile games, ideally RPG/midcore, with end-to-end ownership of major features, progression, monetization or product roadmaps.
  • Strong fluency in RPG mechanics and meta systems: progression, power curves, collection, PvP/social, seasons and passes, and strong mobile marketability instincts.
  • Ideally, you’ve taken a title from concept/pre-launch through launch and LiveOps, or shaped product direction across multiple titles.

LiveOps & Execution

  • Deep LiveOps experience, understanding how events, content, progression and monetization work together to drive engagement and repeat spend.
  • Strong track record owning features end-to-end: identify, build, ship, measure and iterate, with a practical understanding of what a live team can realistically ship and maintain, balancing ambition with feasibility.

Leadership & Ways of working

  • Strong cross-functional leadership, able to align Design, Publishing, Data, Economy, UA, Growth and external studios around the product direction.
  • A strategist and builder: able to set direction and lead others, while remaining highly hands-on with the game, systems and data.
  • Thrives in lean, fast-moving, high-autonomy teams with quick tests, short feedback loops and high ownership

Our Culture

At Homa, we prioritize talent, energy, and determination over traditional credentials. We’re building a global community of brilliant, driven people who think boldly, move fast, and push boundaries. We believe true innovation comes from diverse perspectives, deep collaboration, and curiosity without limits. Our culture is grounded in four core values:

  • Ambition: We strive for the best - we don’t settle for “good enough.”
  • Humility: We recognize that we are always learning, we can always improve and grow.
  • Curiosity: We continuously seek the “why” behind the “what”.
  • Focus: Our curiosity takes us deeper, not wider - we dive deep into the details.

Benefits

Building great games starts with building a great place to work. Here’s what you can expect:

  • 🏥 Comprehensive Benefits: Depending on your location, you’ll enjoy a range of perks such as insurance, meal vouchers, public transport, gym memberships, and more.
  • 🏢 Paris HQ Access: Enjoy a desk at our private office in a well-located WeWork building that will give you access to WeWork perks like rooftop view and designed coworking spaces.
  • 🌍 Coworking Access: You will have access to WeWork spaces throughout Europe, along with all their perks and professional office environments.
  • 🌐 Global Team: Collaborate in English with top-tier talent from 35+ countries, spanning Europe, the UK, the US, and more. Diversity fuels our creativity and innovation.
  • ✈️ Team Gatherings: We value time together beyond the screen. Join us for occasional team gatherings, off-site retreats (Workations as we name them) to connect, recharge, and celebrate.
  • 📈 Performance Reviews: We’re committed to your growth. Every six months, we reflect on your progress, recognize your achievements, and align on clear development goals.
  • 💻 Equipment Support: From day one, we’ll provide everything you need to do your best work, including a home office setup allowance if you're working remotely.

Where We Hire

Our HQ in Paris is a vibrant hub of creativity, collaboration, and connection. From rooftop lunches and coffee chats to after-work apéros and community events, we’ve designed a space people genuinely enjoy - all within a cozy WeWork filled with good energy (and snacks).

We also have incredible team members across Europe - from Spain and Turkey to Germany, North Macedonia, Poland, the UK, and more. Whether you’re working from a sunny WeWork in Barcelona or your home setup in Warsaw, you’re fully part of our culture. To keep collaboration smooth, we primarily hire within European time zones (UTC to UTC+3). If you're based there - or planning to be - we’d love to hear from you!

Please note: this is one remote position open to multiple countries, not multiple openings.

About the role:

We're hiring for Self-Managed Experience (SMX) — the team responsible for making Camunda 8 deployable in a self-service way for customers who run their own infrastructure. SMX covers two areas of work: installation artifacts (Helm chart, Docker Compose, C8Run) and reference architectures & cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, Azure).

This role sits primarily on the installation artifacts side — building, maintaining, and releasing the artifacts that ship Camunda 8 to every self-managed customer. You'll be fully embedded in that area day-to-day, but you'll work alongside the reference-architecture side of the team regularly, and SMX is actively working toward enabling every engineer to review and contribute across both stacks over time.

SMX is also shifting from a purely artifact- and ops-focused team toward one in which engineers bring customer judgment and product sense alongside technical depth. That means engaging directly with the teams closest to customers — Support, Consulting, Presales — and using that signal to help shape what we prioritize, not just executing a fully-specced ticket.

You'll find plenty of room to leave your own footprint: deployment automation, software and infrastructure testing, multi-region setups, and developer experience are all live areas of investment as the team matures from "basic install" toward full-lifecycle ownership (upgrades, backup/restore, disaster recovery).

What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Engage directly with internal customer-facing teams (Support, Consulting, Presales) to understand real deployment problems, and use that signal to help shape what gets prioritized — not just how it gets built. Collaborate with Development Teams, Product Management, QA, and Documentation to ship integrated, tested, and documented releases.

  • Taken on your first medic rotation slot and support tickets to understand the stack, customer challenges, and deployment environments.

  • Improved onboarding or documentation, turning your own ramp-up experience into concrete improvements.

  • Contributed to artifact fixes, CI/CD enhancements, or test automation that strengthens release quality.

  • Deliver structural improvement initiatives — a feature request, or a test/release improvement.

  • Built working relationships with engineering, QA, and product peers, and started building context on the reference-architecture side of the team.

  • Started forming your own view of a customer pain point from firsthand signal (support tickets, consulting feedback), not just from a ticket description.

What You Bring:

  • Ability and/or willingness to use our product, with genuine curiosity about the customer problem behind a ticket — comfortable asking "should we build this" as well as "how do we build this."

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.description:
About Waniwani

Waniwani builds the infrastructure that distributes insurance and banking products through AI assistants. We raised an $8M seed led by Seedcamp and work with large European banks and insurers. Each enterprise deal has to be scoped, architected, and deployed into a regulated environment. This role owns the layer between a signed deal and a live deployment.

The role

  • Customer workshops, discovery, and requirements (35%). Run technical discovery and workshops with each client, and translate their needs into clear, buildable product requirements for our sales, ops, and engineering teams. Flag what we need to build to support a given setup, such as client self-hosting.

  • Solution architecture and documentation (35%). Design the end-to-end MCP flow and integration architecture for each client, including hosted versus on-premise scenarios, and produce the technical documentation enterprise clients require (BPI France alone is roughly 50 docs).

  • Procurement, security, and delivery oversight (30%). Use our existing compliance library (SOC 2 program, DPAs, prior questionnaire answers) to complete security questionnaires, handle security committees and data-residency questions, and drive procurement to completion. Oversee the MCP deployment itself, which our freelancer network implements.

Across all three, you build the reusable kit that makes this repeatable: scoping templates, architecture patterns, and a procurement answer library.

Objectives

  • 90 days: own scoping and procurement response for active deals, with the reusable kit used on at least one live deal end to end.

  • 6 months: run the full signed-to-live pipeline, including architecture decisions and procurement ownership, without founders in the critical path.

  • 12 months: a repeatable delivery process with patterns reused across clients, and a case for the first hire under this role.

Requirements

  • You are technically credible: you read code, reason fluently about integrations and the MCP and agent stack, and can scope and oversee a deployment. This is not a hands-on production-coding role; implementation is handled by our freelancer network.

  • You are comfortable leading technical conversations with enterprise clients.

  • You can drive a security questionnaire or procurement process to completion from existing documentation.

  • You have worked in or near regulated industries (finance, insurance) and understand compliance and data residency requirements.

  • You work well in ambiguity across sales, ops, and engineering, and ramp into new domains quickly.

  • You have an interest in the MCP and agent stack.

  • You are open to traveling from time to time across Europe and the US to meet clients.

What this role is not

  • A backend engineering role. You will work with clients most of the week.

  • A pure pre-sales role. You own architecture, requirements, and delivery oversight, not only the pitch.

  • A slideware role. You need real technical depth, even though you are not writing production code day to day.

Practicalities

  • Remote-first, based in Europe. Expect travel roughly once a month, primarily Paris, London, and Madrid, with US travel around the 6-month mark. Being able to come to Paris occasionally is a plus but not required.

  • First hire in this function, working directly with the founders and the engineering team.

Process

  • Intro call with our talent partner.

  • 30-minute conversation with Max, our CTO.

  • Work sample based on a real client scenario (live session): scope the flow, draft the architecture, and handle a mock procurement Q&A.

  • Discussions with Robin, our CEO, Luiza, and members of the tech team.

  • Reference checks.

jobs.description:
Role: Senior Product Designer

Company: SimpleStudy

Location: Remote, Europe (preferably Western / continental); relocation to Lisbon possible

Job Type: Full-time

About SimpleStudy

SimpleStudy is an AI exam prep platform that students find and choose for themselves.

In some numbers:

  • 1.5M+ students across the UK, Ireland, Brazil, South Africa, and Australia

  • 40–50k new students every week

  • Web, mobile, and desktop apps

  • $4M seed round with investors from Strava, OpenAI, and Meta

The traction came fast. Now the company is refounding: rebuilding the brand, the design language, and the product experience from scratch. The product grew like a Jenga tower, one feature on top of another. The job now is to rebuild it as a pyramid.

The team is ~30 people, remote with a Lisbon office — lean, product-led, and deliberately not a typical edtech company.

You'll report to José, the Founding Designer, and work with him as a partner. José tends to lead early framing and direction. You bring strong craft and take the work to the finish line, in close sync with engineering. You both shape the new design language, and you push back with a better idea when you see one.

What you are expected to do:

  • Shape the new design language and brand: design system, rebrand, and the new mobile app.

  • Own the full design process — from an ambiguous problem to a polished, shipped solution.

  • Drive the consumer experience: onboarding, social features, retention, and the learning loop.

  • Work in close sync with engineers and PM, not as a handoff step - polish the implementation together until it feels right.

  • Bring your own initiatives and say "no, but…" when you see a better way.

  • Raise the bar for the whole design team.

What you need to succeed:

  • High craft — your visual work is polished and intentional; the details reveal your thinking.

  • Storytelling over process — you take an ambiguous problem, frame it, and make it simple. Your portfolio shows artifacts, not diagrams; it has a point of view.

  • Consumer instinct — you've shipped B2C products that people chose to use. You understand product metrics and use them as input, but you lead with feel and craft.

  • Opinions with backbone — you have a design philosophy, can defend it under pushback, and bring your own initiatives. You don't wait to be told what to build.

  • Energy and curiosity — you're an interesting person with a life outside work, and you leave people energised after a conversation.

  • English — fluent, written and spoken.

What would be a plus:

  • A standout specialty: prototyping, illustration, animation, or motion.

  • Experience with social or viral product mechanics.

  • Background at consumer companies like Spotify or Strava.

  • Early-stage or founding designer experience.

  • Comfortable in code: prototyping or polishing the front end.

What you get:

  • Build from scratch, at scale — a new design language for a product already used by 1.5M+ students.

  • A strong partner - work closely with José, the Founding Designer (ex-Shopify), with direct access to the founders.

  • Equity — generous stock options, early enough for them to matter.

  • Remote Europe — work from where you choose, with in-person meetups three times a year; relocation support if you want to move to Lisbon.

  • Competitive salary — no fixed budget, flexible.

How to apply:

A deck or a walkthrough video is fine. Show the work, keep it curated.
